name: BEP (Bleomycin / Etoposide / Cisplatin)
cyclesNote: 3-4 cycles depending on stage/risk for malignant ovarian germ-cell tumors.

source.nccn: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Ovarian germ-cell tumors (general reference)

institution.provenance: StewardMD DRAFT germ-cell backbone authored in-house from standard-of-care oncology; experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated.

premedications.name: Antiemetic prophylaxis
premedications.notes: Cisplatin is highly emetogenic; use a 3-drug (NK1 + 5HT3 + steroid) regimen.

premedications.name: Hydration
premedications.notes: Vigorous pre- and post-cisplatin IV hydration with magnesium/potassium repletion to protect renal function.

supportiveCare: Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity: baseline and periodic pulmonary assessment, track cumulative bleomycin dose, and stop for early interstitial changes.
Cisplatin nephro-, oto- and neurotoxicity: audiometry and renal monitoring; consider growth-factor support for neutropenia.
monitoring: CBC before each cycle and mid-cycle
renal function and electrolytes before each cisplatin dose
pulmonary symptoms/exam before each bleomycin dose
tumor markers (AFP, beta-hCG, LDH) each cycle

drugs.name: Bleomycin
drugs.notes: Bleomycin 30 units IV weekly on days 1, 8 and 15 each 21-day cycle. Track cumulative lifetime dose and monitor for pulmonary toxicity; hold for early interstitial change. Authored in StewardMD's words from standard-of-care oncology (NCCN/DeVita general reference).

drugs.name: Etoposide
drugs.notes: Etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1-5 every 21 days. Myelosuppressive; small long-term secondary-leukemia risk. Authored in StewardMD's words from standard-of-care oncology (NCCN/DeVita general reference).

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.notes: Cisplatin 20 mg/m2 IV on days 1-5 every 21 days with vigorous hydration. Nephro-, oto- and neurotoxic; monitor renal function, electrolytes and audiometry. Authored in StewardMD's words from standard-of-care oncology (NCCN/DeVita general reference).
